hints: Focus on finding the chiral centre in mevalonic acid first, look for a carbon with four different groups attached.
Notice the central carbon bonded to $\text{OH}$ and $\text{CH}_3$ has two different $\text{CH}_2$ chains on either side, so it is chiral to start with.
Consider which reaction could make those two side chains identical, so that central carbon ends up with two matching groups and loses its chirality.
walkthrough:
**Identify the chiral centre in the starting material**

Mevalonic acid is $\text{HO}_2\text{C-CH}_2\text{-C(OH)(CH}_3\text{)-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-OH}$. Look at each carbon.

The central carbon is bonded to $\text{OH}$, $\text{CH}_3$, $\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ and $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. That is four different groups, so it is chiral.

**Recall what each reagent does**

Esterification (A) only changes $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ to $\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$. Sodium (C) only changes $\text{OH}$ to $\text{O}^-\text{Na}^+$. $\text{PCl}_5$ (D) only changes $\text{OH}$ to $\text{Cl}$.

None of these change the carbon skeleton, so the four groups stay different and the centre stays chiral.

**Apply strong oxidation with dichromate**

Heating with $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}/\text{H}^+$ oxidises the primary alcohol $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ all the way to a carboxylic acid $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$. The tertiary alcohol does not oxidise.

$$\text{HO}_2\text{C-CH}_2\text{-C(OH)(CH}_3\text{)-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{HO}_2\text{C-CH}_2\text{-C(OH)(CH}_3\text{)-CH}_2\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$$

**Check chirality of the product**

The new product is 3-hydroxy-3-methylpentanedioic acid. The central carbon is now bonded to $\text{OH}$, $\text{CH}_3$, and two identical $\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ groups.

With two identical groups it is no longer chiral, and all other carbons are $\text{CH}_2$, so the molecule has no chiral carbon atom.

options.A: Heating with $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}/\text{H}^+$ gives esterification of the carboxylic acid to $\text{CH}_3\text{O}_2\text{C-CH}_2\text{-C(OH)(CH}_3\text{)-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$. The central carbon still has four different groups, so it remains chiral.
options.B: Strong oxidation converts the terminal primary alcohol to a second carboxylic acid, giving $\text{HO}_2\text{C-CH}_2\text{-C(OH)(CH}_3\text{)-CH}_2\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$. The central carbon now has two identical $\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ arms, so it is achiral and the whole molecule has no chiral centre.
options.C: Na reacts with the acidic protons of $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ and $\text{-OH}$ to give $\text{-CO}_2^-\text{Na}^+$ and $\text{-O}^-\text{Na}^+$ salts. The connectivity of the carbon skeleton is unchanged, so the central carbon still has four different groups and stays chiral.
options.D: $\text{PCl}_5$ replaces every $\text{OH}$ with $\text{Cl}$, giving an acyl chloride plus alkyl chlorides: $\text{ClOC-CH}_2\text{-C(Cl)(CH}_3\text{)-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{Cl}$. The central carbon still has four different groups ($\text{Cl}$, $\text{CH}_3$, and two different $\text{CH}_2$ chains), so it remains chiral.
